articles.headline: New India Co-operative Bank’s earliest disclosed warning was asset quality, not a market call
articles.dek: The replay places an NNPA action-zone breach well before the recorded event. That is a filing-period signal, not proof of a tradable market warning or a forensic explanation of a fraud-masked failure.
articles.body_markdown:
This is not current news and not a forecast. It is a historical replay of New India Co-operative Bank, whose recorded event date is 2025-02-13. The narrow thesis is that the institution’s balance sheet should have shown stress first through disclosed asset quality: an RBI action-zone breach associated with net non-performing assets, or NNPA, appeared before the event. The thesis does not say a market price predicted the outcome, and it does not claim that the reported ratio establishes the underlying cause.

The distinction is essential. A filing-period signal says what the replay finds in reported information at a reporting date, with an assumed availability clock where necessary. A market-price signal would describe what a tradable instrument repriced when. A model derivation would turn inputs into a score, tier, or estimated risk measure. Those are different objects. Treating one as evidence for another is the fastest way to make a retrospective warning look more useful than it was.

## The record before the event

The first recorded supervisory action-zone trigger is the 2021-03-31 period end, identified as FY2021. The breached lens was NNPA. Because the record lacks an explicit publication clock, the replay assigns a knowledge-time proxy of 2021-05-30 under its period-end-plus-60-days convention. The stated lead to the 2025-02-13 event is 44 months.

That is a filing-period chronology, not a claim that an investor received a verified warning on the period-end date. The replay explicitly uses an availability proxy: an explicit publication clock when present, otherwise period end plus 60 days. Its historical evidence is labelled PERIOD_END_PROXY_CONSTRUCTION_PIT, its lead times are explicitly optimistic, and it lacks a bitemporal input contract. It is **not validated-backtest eligible** and **not real-money eligible**.

The [New India Co-operative Bank replay](https://liquilens.in/replay/new-india-co-operative-bank/) and the [Failure Radar board](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/board) identify the institution as fraud-masked. That label is not a conclusion about the nature, timing, or scope of misconduct. It is a methodological warning: filings later shown falsified can look compliant to a threshold engine, while disclosed deterioration can fail to capture the hidden condition that ultimately mattered.

## What the lenses saw

The PCA/SAF-style lens recorded NNPA as the first action-zone signal. The funding lens recorded no first signal. Those findings have sharply different meanings from a clean bill of health. The first is a disclosed threshold breach in the replay. The second is not evidence of stable funding: the funding lens only observes institutions with a usable liability series, and missing liability disclosure can prevent a signal from being observed.

The validation summaries provide limited context. Among 15 failed institutions in the PCA summary, 5 entered an action zone first, with a median lead of 41 months. In the funding summary, 10 of 15 failed institutions had liability disclosures; 4 had a funding signal fire first, with a median lead of 38 months. These are descriptive replay outcomes, not conditional failure probabilities and not proof that the same mechanism dominated at New India.

The model evidence is also weaker than a polished score can imply. The temporal diagnostic AUC is 0.645, below its 0.65 gate. The diagnostic is explicitly not promotable: construction-PIT diagnostics cannot promote. The conformal alarm remains a diagnostic, but its historical tier wiring is suspended and it has no score or tier authority pending prospective revalidation. A retrospective narrative cannot cure a failed gate.

## Why the warning mattered

An NNPA action-zone breach matters as a balance-sheet signal because impaired disclosed assets can make collections less dependable and loss recognition more consequential. If pressure persists, capital absorption and management flexibility may become more important. That can affect confidence in the institution’s ability to absorb losses or adjust funding.

But that is a mechanism, not an established causal sequence for this bank. The dossier does not show that funding stress followed NNPA stress, nor does it establish that asset quality was the decisive source of the recorded event. The defensible conclusion is smaller: NNPA was the earliest documented supervisory-risk signal in this replay.

## The strongest counter-case

The counter-case can defeat the thesis. Because this institution is fraud-masked, the visible ratio may be a poor map of the true balance sheet. The NNPA breach could have been early, late, incomplete, or incidental to a hidden condition. A threshold engine can be useful for disclosed fragility while remaining unable to reconstruct what disclosures concealed.

The 44-month lead is also too long to demonstrate event timing. A warning can identify vulnerability without identifying imminence. The proxy availability convention may make the lead look cleaner than a genuinely point-in-time research record would permit. And the absence of a funding first signal may reflect missing or unusable liability information rather than an asset-led path.

The steel-manned verdict is therefore not that NNPA caused the event. It is that NNPA was the first disclosed warning available in this construction-PIT record, subject to a fraud-masking limitation strong enough to prevent causal certainty.

## What today's board shares

Today’s board is not a current scorecard for New India Co-operative Bank; failed institutions are replayed on the Evidence tab. As of 2026-10-08, the comparison set contains 0 red institutions, 0 orange, 1 yellow, and 2 green. Belstar Microfinance Limited is yellow with a score of 77.8; Annapurna Finance Private Limited and Arohan Financial Services Limited are green at 96.5 and 97.1. Their filing as-of date is 2026-03-31 and their stated age is 7 months.

Those are model-derived board outputs, not market-price signals and not credit ratings. The board excludes 35 stale institutions. Nothing older than 183 days for quarterly filings or 400 days for annual filings is presented as current. Omission is not reassurance; institutions without vetted dossiers are absent by design rather than scored from memory.

The market layer is available and fresh in clock terms, dated 2026-10-07 and retrieved on 2026-10-08. Yet it has 0 admitted canonical records out of 25, and no publication or tier authority. Its [market evidence index](https://api.liquilens.in/api/evidence/markets) may support investigation, but cannot support a market-derived institutional tier claim.

## The next falsifiable test

This thesis fails if a fully time-stamped authoritative record shows that the relevant disclosed NNPA condition did not enter the action zone before 2025-02-13, or was not available by the assumed 2021-05-30 proxy date. It weakens if reliable contemporaneous liability disclosures reveal an earlier funding signal missed by this replay.

The prospective test is to preserve original publication times, revisions, and later evidence of falsification, then test whether action-zone breaches add timely information beyond funding and forensic evidence. Until that exists, the 44-month figure is a historical replay lead, not an investable lead time.

## Follow the pressure chain

The diagnostic chain is conditional: impaired disclosed assets may reduce expected collections; reduced collections may increase loss-recognition and capital pressure; capital pressure may narrow balance-sheet flexibility; narrowing flexibility may make funding confidence more consequential. No arrow is asserted as a fact about every institution.

LiquiLens covers **institution and lender balance-sheet risk**. [Seiche](https://api.seiche.info/api/overview) covers **system dollar-funding capacity**. [Undertow](https://api.seiche.info/undertow/board.json) covers market liquidity and executable exit capacity. These are separate research boundaries: system conditions, an institution’s disclosed condition, and the ability to exit a position are not interchangeable confirmations.

## Sources, method, and limits

The principal records are the [Failure Radar board](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/board), [historical validation file](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/validation), [New India replay](https://liquilens.in/replay/new-india-co-operative-bank/), [market evidence index](https://api.liquilens.in/api/evidence/markets), [Seiche overview](https://api.seiche.info/api/overview), [Undertow board](https://api.seiche.info/undertow/board.json), and [US NDFI diagnostic](https://api.liquilens.in/api/us-radar/ndfi). The US diagnostic is context only and supplies no evidence about New India.

The tier rule fuses independently replayed components for presentation. Stale, future-dated, or unclocked market readings can remain visible but have no signal or tier authority. Most importantly, fraud masking means neither an apparently calm disclosure record nor an observed ratio can substitute for forensic reconstruction.

This is not a credit rating. Research and market data, not investment advice.

articles.headline: Nedungadi Bank’s capital breach was an early warning, not a timetable
articles.dek: The replay identifies a CRAR action-zone breach well before Nedungadi Bank’s default. It supports a narrow historical finding about a filing-period capital signal, while leaving funding, market pricing and causation unresolved.
articles.body_markdown:
*This is a historical replay, not current news and not a forecast. Similar mechanisms do not imply the same outcome.*

Nedungadi Bank is the clearest answer in this record to the question of which balance sheet should have felt stress first: its reported capital position entered an RBI action zone before its eventual default. But that conclusion needs boundaries. The breach is a filing-period signal, reconstructed using a publication-time proxy. It is not a contemporaneous market-price signal, and it is not a model-derived probability of default. The replay records an early warning; it does not prove a complete causal sequence.

## The record before the event

Nedungadi Bank defaulted on 2002-11-02. Its first documented PCA action-zone event was a CRAR breach for the period ending 1999-03-31, identified as FY1999. The PCA record labels the event `threshold_1` and assigns a knowledge-time proxy of 1999-05-30. The measured lead to default is 41 months.

That chronology is the core fact. The period end says when the reported condition existed in the replayed record. The knowledge-time proxy says when an outside observer may have been able to know it under the construction rule. Where no explicit publication clock exists, the system uses period end plus 60 days. It is therefore inappropriate to treat 1999-03-31 as a verified real-time observation date.

The funding lens supplies no offsetting result. Nedungadi is marked unscoreable for funding, with no first signal and no measured funding lead. That does not show that funding was stable. It shows that the available liability disclosure was insufficient for this lens. Missing information is an evidence boundary, not reassurance.

## What the lenses saw

The PCA lens saw a CRAR threshold breach. The funding lens did not produce a scoreable reading. The market layer available for the current board is a separate dataset, dated 2026-10-06, and cannot be retrofitted into the Nedungadi chronology. Conflating these layers would turn distinct forms of evidence into a false confirmation.

A filing-period capital breach is a reported regulatory-threshold condition. A market-price signal would instead be a repricing observation. The dossier describes the Merton PD specifically as a market repricing signal, not a calibrated failure frequency. A model output is another category again: it is a derivation from specified inputs and rules, not direct evidence that a bank has failed or will fail.

The historical PCA summary covers 15 failed institutions, of which 5 entered an action zone first; its median lead is 41 months. The funding summary has liability disclosures for 10 of those 15 institutions and records funding as the first signal for 4, with a median lead of 38 months. Those comparisons do not establish that capital is always the earliest lens. They show that different disclosed pathways appeared first in different cases.

The India diagnostic spans 48 institutions across two decades and reports that 88.9% of non-fraud failures were flagged, with a median lead of 21.5 months. Yet it is explicitly a filing-availability-proxied construction-PIT diagnostic. It is not validated-backtest eligible, not real-money eligible, and does not have a bitemporal input contract.

## Why the warning mattered

The economic significance of the breach is limited but intelligible: the dossier identifies capital as the first documented action-zone pressure point at Nedungadi. A capital threshold is closer to loss-absorption capacity than a broad narrative about confidence or market access. It can therefore be useful in triage as a question for investigation: what changed in the reported buffer, and did other disclosed constraints follow?

The quadrant rule treats an RBI action-zone breach as sufficient for the highest screen category. That is a screening rule, not a finding of causation. Other routes to concern include reported loss levels, deterioration, funding flags, forensic indicators and fresh authoritative market drawdown signals. The rule identifies a reason to look harder; it does not provide timing certainty or a complete failure explanation.

The model evidence should make readers more restrained, not more confident. The leave-one-institution-out hazard AUC is 0.752, while the disclosure heuristic reaches 0.799 on the same held-out rows. The temporal diagnostic AUC is 0.645, below the 0.65 gate, and is diagnostic only. Construction-PIT diagnostics cannot promote.

## The strongest counter-case

The counter-case can defeat the thesis. A capital action-zone breach may be an early regulatory marker without becoming the decisive driver of failure. The 41-month lead is particularly important: it is evidence against reading the breach as a countdown. A bank might repair reported capital, alter its balance sheet, or receive support. The dossier supplies no institution-specific evidence that the CRAR breach itself caused Nedungadi’s default.

The sample also weakens any claim of universality. Only 5 of 15 failed institutions entered the PCA action zone first. Funding was first among 4 institutions with the relevant liability disclosures. And Nedungadi’s funding lens is unavailable, so this case cannot establish whether capital preceded a liability-side deterioration or merely became observable first.

Timing is another serious objection. The replay relies on an explicit publication clock where present and otherwise a conservative period-end plus 60-day proxy. Even so, the dossier says lead times may be optimistic. Filings later shown to be falsified can make institutions appear compliant to a threshold engine; the forensic screen owns that problem. Nedungadi is marked fraud-masked false, but that label does not remove the general limitation.

## What today's board shares

Today’s board is not an extension of the Nedungadi result. As of 2026-10-07, the Failure Radar shows 0 red names, 0 orange names, 1 yellow name and 2 green names. Belstar Microfinance Limited is yellow, while Annapurna Finance Private Limited and Arohan Financial Services Limited are green. Their listed filings are as of 2026-03-31 and are 7 months old.

The board excludes 35 stale institutions. Its presentation rule does not treat quarterly filings older than 183 days, or annual filings older than 400 days, as current. Institutions without vetted dossiers are absent by design. This makes the roster a screened subset rather than a claim about every lender.

Current market data are fresh, but their display, publication and tier use are not approved for every expected canonical record. The admitted canonical-record count is 0/25. Market-derived readings therefore cannot validate a current tier in this article.

## The next falsifiable test

The thesis should be tested prospectively, not defended through a single replay. Preserve the original filing vintage and exact public availability time for each new disclosure. Track capital, funding and forensic signals separately. Report stale and missing institutions as exclusions rather than as negative observations. Then test whether action-zone breaches identify independently observed balance-sheet stress earlier than comparable non-breaching institutions.

The thesis fails if capital thresholds do not add timely information once publication timing, missing liability disclosures, revised filings and forensic masking are handled honestly. It also fails if later information is required to make the earlier warning look useful.

## Follow the pressure chain

For Nedungadi, the documented chain is short: a reported CRAR breach, followed 41 months later by default. Any middle link between those facts is an interpretation, not a recorded institution-specific event in this dossier.

LiquiLens covers **institution and lender balance-sheet risk**. [Seiche](https://api.seiche.info/api/overview) covers **system dollar-funding capacity**. articles.headline: Rupee Co-operative Bank: the warning was a blank record, not an early signal
articles.dek: The replay cannot establish that Rupee Co-operative Bank’s balance sheet felt stress first. It establishes a stricter lesson: when liability disclosures and vetted inputs are absent, an institution is outside the lens—not safely inside it.
articles.body_markdown:
*This is a historical replay, not current news and not a forecast. It examines Rupee Co-operative Bank, whose recorded default date is 2022-09-22. Similar mechanisms do not imply the same outcome.*

The most defensible answer to the desk question is uncomfortable. The supplied record does not show that Rupee Co-operative Bank should have felt financial stress before another institution, nor does it identify which balance-sheet channel tightened first. It shows that the bank was not scoreable through the funding lens and has no recorded PCA action-zone entry in this replay. That is a coverage boundary, not reassurance.

This distinction separates three things that are too easily blended. A filing-period signal is an observation from reported disclosures, available only when those disclosures exist and can be dated. A market-price signal is a repricing observation; in this framework, the Merton PD is explicitly a market repricing signal, not a calibrated failure frequency. A model derivation combines eligible inputs under a published rule. None may fill a missing liability series, and none may use a later default to manufacture an earlier warning.

## The record before the event

Rupee Co-operative Bank is classified as an urban co-operative bank. Its funding record is explicitly marked unscoreable. The dossier supplies no first funding signal and no funding lead time. Its PCA replay likewise supplies no first action-zone entry and no lead time. Fraud masking is marked false, but that field is not proof that every relevant condition was observable or that a forensic review was complete.

The key fact is therefore an absence of eligible evidence, not evidence of strength. A subsequent default date cannot be used to infer that a reported capital, asset-quality, funding, or market measure must have deteriorated beforehand. That would reverse the evidentiary sequence and turn the outcome into an input.

The historical record has a further timing limitation. India is described as a filing-availability-proxied construction-PIT diagnostic rather than a bitemporal input contract. Where an explicit publication clock is absent, the framework uses period end plus 60 days. Its lead times are therefore described as optimistic. The evidence is neither validated-backtest eligible nor real-money eligible.

The proper case statement is narrow: Rupee was outside the scoreable funding lens, and no PCA lead is recorded. A fuller contemporaneous record could alter that finding. The supplied dossier cannot tell us whether such a record would have shown earlier stress.

## What the lenses saw

The PCA and funding lenses address different possible routes to fragility. The PCA/SAF replay reconstructs public-disclosure regulatory tripwires. Across 15 failed institutions, 5 entered the action zone first, with median lead of 41 months. The funding lens depends on liability disclosure: among the same 15 failed institutions, 10 had liability disclosures, 4 saw the funding signal fire first, and median lead was 38 months.

Those figures do not support an inference about Rupee. They demonstrate why eligibility must be preserved. A funding lens can only inspect institutions that disclose the relevant liability series. Rupee is explicitly outside that population. A blank field means that the lens has no scoreable input; it does not mean funding was sound.

The broader India diagnostic covers 48 institutions across two decades and reports that 88.9% of non-fraud failures were flagged, with median lead of 21.5 months. Yet it retains the same construction-PIT limitation. The hazard model also does not clear its stated temporal diagnostic gate: AUC is 0.645 against a 0.65 threshold and is diagnostic only. The held-out heuristic comparison is stronger than the hazard result on the stated rows. These are reasons to resist converting a replay statistic into a claim of prospective predictive power.

## Why the warning mattered

The warning here was procedural. A balance-sheet process becomes misleading if it silently maps missing information to a benign tier. The correct output for an unscoreable institution is a visible exception: identify the absent disclosure, state which lens is disabled, and decide whether further diligence is necessary before relying on the screen.

In principle, financial pressure can travel through asset quality and capital, liability structure and funding, or market access. But this case file does not establish that any one of those links led Rupee’s path to default. A filing-period measure, if it existed, would be a reported-condition signal. A market-price measure would be a separate repricing signal. A model score would be a derivation from eligible inputs. They are not interchangeable evidence.

The operational implication is not to assign a synthetic probability. It is to ask what decision is being made despite the missing record. That is especially important when a screen is being used comparatively: an institution with sparse disclosures should not appear safer merely because its inputs cannot trigger a rule.

## The strongest counter-case

The strongest counter-case can defeat any expansive thesis. Rupee’s missing scoreability makes it unhelpful for ranking which institution should have felt stress first. There is no supplied dated deterioration, no scoreable liability trail, and no recorded PCA entry. The replay cannot claim the model would have warned, cannot claim that funding pressure preceded the event, and cannot claim a precise lead time.

The same restraint applies to market information. The market layer is fresh by its stated clock, but it has no publication, admission, or tier authority. Its canonical-record admission count is zero out of 25 because rights, display, model-gate, and tier-use approvals are not in place. It may not be used to strengthen a Rupee conclusion.

That counter-case does not turn missing information into an all-clear. It establishes the opposite governance rule: the case is outside the comparative model claim. A blank cannot prove fragility, but it also cannot earn a green label.

## What today's board shares

The current Failure Radar has 1 yellow, 2 green, and no red or orange institutions. Belstar Microfinance Limited is yellow at 77.8. Annapurna Finance Private Limited and Arohan Financial Services Limited are green at 96.5 and 97.1. Their listed filing date is 2026-03-31, with an age of 7 months on the board date. There are also 35 excluded stale cases.

These are not exhaustive lender rankings. The method presents current institutions only with a fresh vetted public dossier, excluding quarterly filings older than 183 days and annual filings older than 400 days from current presentation. That discipline prevents false freshness; it does not establish safety among excluded names.

The relevant product boundary is exact. [LiquiLens](https://liquilens.in/articles/) covers **institution and lender balance-sheet risk**. [Seiche](https://api.seiche.info/api/overview) covers **system dollar-funding capacity**. [Undertow](https://api.seiche.info/undertow/board.json) covers **market liquidity and executable exit capacity**. The research boundary follows from those definitions: system context or exit conditions cannot substitute for a missing institution-level disclosure record.

## The next falsifiable test

This article’s limited thesis can be disproved by contemporaneously available, vetted Rupee filings or liability disclosures that establish dated deterioration before 2022-09-22. The evidence would need to show eligibility for the relevant lens, the relevant reported inputs, and a threshold crossing under the stated publication clock. A documented RBI action-zone breach could also change the PCA finding.

If instead a complete contemporaneous record showed no threshold breach under those rules, the narrower conclusion would survive: these disclosed lenses did not publicly foreshadow the event. Either result is superior to retrospective scoring.

A live investigation should follow reported asset quality and capital, then liability structure and funding disclosures, and only then authorized market access evidence. Each step must retain its label. A regulatory tripwire is not a default forecast. A market repricing signal is not a calibrated failure frequency. A model derivation is not an observed balance-sheet fact.

For Rupee, the chain breaks at the evidence stage. The appropriate response is an explicit coverage exception and renewed diligence, not a synthetic tier. This is not investment advice.

articles.headline: CKP Co-operative Bank replay: when a missing warning is not an all-clear
articles.dek: CKP Co-operative Bank’s historical file does not establish a clean advance balance-sheet alarm before default. It instead shows why an unscoreable institution must remain an observability problem, not be recast as a calm one.
articles.body_markdown:
*This is a historical replay, not current news and not a forecast. CKP Co-operative Bank defaulted on 2020-04-30. The Failure Radar snapshot is as of 2026-10-05. The market pack is as of 2026-10-01 and was retrieved on 2026-10-05. Those current reference dates do not change the historical nature of the CKP record.*

CKP Co-operative Bank is a hard test of the proposition that a balance-sheet screen can identify which institution should feel financial stress first. The dossier does not show that a PCA-style threshold or funding signal supplied a clean, measurable advance warning before its default. It also does not support the opposite conclusion: that the absence of such a signal was evidence of resilience.

That distinction is more than a caveat. A filing-period signal says what can be reconstructed from a reported balance-sheet record under a stated availability convention. A market-price signal is a separate repricing observation, and this dossier does not authorize market-derived display, model, or tier use. A model derivation is a rule applied to the inputs; it is not an independently observed institutional fact. CKP’s central result is therefore non-observability, rather than a demonstrated clean bill of health or a demonstrated early alarm.

## The record before the event

CKP Co-operative Bank is classified as a UCB and has a default date of 2020-04-30. Its PCA record contains no first action zone and no measured lead months. Its funding lens is not scoreable, with no first signal and no measured lead months. The file is not fraud-masked.

Those are deliberately narrow statements. They do not document a PCA action-zone breach that can be presented as the first public warning. They do not document a funding signal. Nor do they establish that the underlying balance sheet was sound. The dedicated [CKP replay](https://liquilens.in/replay/ckp-co-operative-bank/) and [Failure Radar board](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/board) are constrained reconstructions, not contemporaneous credit opinions.

The historical evidence status is `PERIOD_END_PROXY_CONSTRUCTION_PIT`. It is not eligible as a validated backtest, is **not eligible for real-money use**, and lacks a bitemporal input contract. Where an explicit publication clock exists, it is used; otherwise availability is set at period end plus 60 days. The dossier explicitly says lead times may be optimistic.

That is a research boundary, not a footnote. A filing-period reconstruction cannot prove that an outside observer possessed, trusted, and could interpret an input on a particular historical date when its availability is proxied. The missing warning is consequently not proof that the warning mechanism failed, nor proof that CKP was calm before the event.

## What the lenses saw

The PCA lens replays public-disclosure versions of the RBI’s PCA/SAF tripwires. In the historical summary, 5 of 15 failed institutions entered an action zone first, with median lead of 41 months. That aggregate result cannot be assigned to CKP: its record has no first action-zone entry.

The funding lens has an even stricter dependency. Of 15 failed institutions, 10 had liability disclosures; a funding signal fired first for 4, with median lead of 38 months. The lens can only see institutions that disclose a liability series. CKP is not scoreable under it. “No funding signal” here means no authorized funding-lens conclusion, not no funding risk.

The broader India diagnostic covers 48 institutions across two decades and reports 88.9% of non-fraud failures flagged, with median lead of 21.5 months. But it carries the same filing-availability-proxied construction-PIT status and optimistic-lead-time warning. The [validation record](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/validation) shows a temporal AUC of 0.645, below the 0.65 diagnostic gate. Its construction-PIT diagnostics cannot promote.

## Why the warning mattered

A balance-sheet mechanism is observable only after relevant information is disclosed, mapped, and admitted to the rule. Asset-quality damage, losses, capital erosion, or funding strain may precede that process. If a liability series is unavailable, the funding channel cannot be scored. If a publication clock is inferred, the apparent lead may overstate what was knowable. If a vetted dossier is absent, the architecture does not score from memory.

CKP therefore identifies an institution-risk boundary: rankable risk and unobservable risk must not be merged into the same reassuring category. LiquiLens covers **institution and lender balance-sheet risk**. In this case, the institution-level evidence does not establish an authorized pre-default ranking. That is not a reason to invent a score; it is a reason not to translate non-scoreability into green.

## The strongest counter-case

The counter-case can defeat a careless version of this thesis. A disciplined screen should not manufacture distress from missing information. CKP has no fraud-masked flag. The dossier reports neither a PCA action-zone entry nor a funding trigger nor measured lead months. Automatically escalating every incomplete file would confuse missingness with demonstrated weakness and could create false positives.

That argument is strong. The method says institutions without vetted dossiers are absent by design, and nothing is scored from memory. The conformal alarm is diagnostic only; its historical tier wiring is suspended and it has no score or tier authority pending prospective revalidation. Those controls prevent a retrospective story from becoming a fabricated signal.

But the counter-case fails if refusal to score is recast as reassurance. “Not scoreable” is a data-state conclusion. It is neither green nor a prediction of failure. CKP supports that limited, but important, conclusion.

## What today's board shares

The current board is separate from CKP’s replay. As of 2026-10-05, it contains 1 yellow and 2 green institutions, with no red or orange tiers. Belstar Microfinance Limited is yellow, while Annapurna Finance Private Limited and Arohan Financial Services Limited are green. Their filings are as of 2026-03-31 and aged 7 months. A further 35 stale institutions are excluded.

The market layer is fresh by its own clock, as of 2026-10-01, but has no publication, admission, or tier authority: admitted canonical records are 0/25. It cannot change tiers. The [market evidence index](https://api.liquilens.in/api/evidence/markets) is context, not an authorized institution signal.

## The next falsifiable test

The thesis is falsifiable. A prospective record would need time-stamped, vetted disclosures for comparable institutions, including liability series where funding analysis is intended. It should then test whether authorized PCA or funding signals precede severe stress using actual publication-time availability rather than a period-end proxy.

articles.headline: New India Co-operative Bank showed a disclosed stress breach before the event — and the fraud boundary is the point
articles.dek: A historical replay finds an NNPA action-zone breach at the FY2021 period end, ahead of the later default date. It supports investigation of disclosed balance-sheet pressure, not confidence that a threshold screen can see through false accounts.
articles.body_markdown:
*This is a historical replay, not current news and not a forecast. It examines the public record before New India Co-operative Bank’s default date of 2025-02-13. Similar mechanisms do not imply the same outcome elsewhere.*

The desk question has a conditional answer. On the disclosed record, New India Co-operative Bank should have drawn attention through an asset-quality signal: an NNPA breach placing it in the RBI PCA/SAF action zone for the period ended 2021-03-31, labelled FY2021. The replay uses 2021-05-30 as its knowledge-time proxy and records a 44-month lead to default.

That is a filing-period signal. It is not proof that the published balance sheet described the institution’s actual condition, and it is not a market-price signal or a model result. The dossier marks this case fraud-masked. That qualification is decisive: a reported threshold crossing warrants investigation, but cannot deliver a forensic account of a bank whose filings may have been unreliable.

## The record before the event

Three clocks must remain separate. The filing period ended on 2021-03-31. Where no explicit publication clock is available, the replay uses period end plus 60 days, producing the 2021-05-30 knowledge-time proxy. The default occurred on 2025-02-13. None is a current-market timestamp, or evidence of what management, supervisors, depositors, or counterparties knew privately.

The PCA/SAF lens replays public disclosure against the RBI’s action-zone tripwires. It can identify a reported threshold breach, not establish causation, reconstruct undisclosed cash movements, assess intent, or verify that the reported inputs were true. The [New India replay](https://liquilens.in/replay/new-india-co-operative-bank/) is evidence of what a disclosure screen could flag from the available record.

Fraud-masked is not a footnote. Institutions whose filings were later shown falsified can appear compliant to a threshold engine. Even this early visible breach cannot establish whether reported deterioration captured the full problem, its first stage, or only part of it. A disclosure warning can be useful and materially incomplete at once.

## What the lenses saw

The PCA/SAF lens saw the NNPA breach. The funding lens produced no first signal for New India. That is missing evidence, not evidence of stable funding: the funding lens only sees institutions that disclose a liability series. No funding signal cannot become a funding all-clear.

Across 15 failed institutions, 5 entered the PCA/SAF action zone first, with a median lead of 41 months. The funding summary has liability disclosures for 10 of those 15 institutions; its signal fired first for 4, with a median lead of 38 months. These are replay descriptions, not prospective accuracy claims.

The wider India diagnostic covers 48 institutions across two decades and says 88.9% of non-fraud failures were flagged, with a median lead of 21.5 months. Yet it is explicitly PERIOD_END_PROXY_CONSTRUCTION_PIT: not eligible as a validated backtest or real-money test, without a bitemporal input contract, and with optimistic lead times. The [validation record](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/validation) and [market evidence index](https://api.liquilens.in/api/evidence/markets) retain those limits.

A model derivation is separate again. The hazard panel contains 205 rows, 9 events, and 27 institutions. A disclosed action-zone breach changes the question from whether an institution looks routine to whether reported asset quality, loss absorption, disclosure quality, and possible funding vulnerability warrant deeper scrutiny.

If reported condition is genuine, pressure may move from asset quality into loss absorption, confidence, funding, and resilience to further losses. But that is a pressure chain, not a demonstrated causal sequence here. New India has an asset-side warning and no funding first signal. Its fraud-masked designation means disclosures may not have measured the actual condition fully. Investigation, rather than a tidy narrative of linear deterioration, is the warranted inference.

The 44-month lead is both meaningful and hazardous. It identifies an early public point at which the disclosed record crossed a regulatory threshold. But a long replay lead can make a threshold engine appear to have seen more than historical filings could reveal.

The counter-case can defeat any broad thesis. New India does not establish that disclosed thresholds reliably forecast institutional failure. An NNPA breach is not proof of insolvency, liquidity failure, misconduct, or an impending default. Timing is another objection. The replay uses explicit publication time when present and otherwise a period-end-plus-60-days proxy. That can make lead times optimistic. Without a bitemporal input contract, the record cannot prove what a live user could access on each historical date. The conformal alarm is diagnostic, with no score or tier authority pending prospective revalidation.

A later event also does not retroactively prove decision usefulness. The heuristic’s stronger held-out AUC and the failed temporal gate limit the model conclusion. The defensible thesis is narrower: disclosed action-zone pressure is a reason to investigate earlier, while fraud and missing disclosures limit what the investigation can infer.

These are published-rule screen outputs, not credit ratings or forecasts. The board excludes 21 stale institutions. A market-price signal would require authorised market evidence, and none establishes Nedungadi’s historical pathway. A model derivation is a rule or diagnostic built over observed records; it is not itself an observed event. Conflating these categories would turn a limited replay into a claim it cannot support.

This historical replay is **not investment advice** and **not a credit rating**.

## The record before the event

The [Nedungadi Bank replay](https://liquilens.in/replay/nedungadi-bank/) records its first PCA/SAF action-zone entry at the 1999-03-31 period end, labelled FY1999. ## What the lenses saw

The PCA lens saw the CRAR breach. The funding lens was not scoreable and produced no first signal. This is a missing-data outcome, not a conclusion that funding was calm, stable, or irrelevant. The funding framework can observe only institutions disclosing a liability series; Nedungadi’s record does not support that lens.

A stronger version of this thesis can fail. The availability convention may flatter apparent warning time. The record lacks a bitemporal input contract and substitutes period end plus 60 days where no explicit publication clock exists. If fully timestamped, contemporaneous liability information had generated an earlier warning, the claim that capital should feel stress first would fail. If a market-price measure had repriced before the filing became knowable, it would answer a different question and also defeat any claim that the filing was the first observable warning overall. The defensible conclusion is narrower: capital was the earliest recorded signal in this replay.

## Follow the pressure chain

The pressure chain supported here stops at disclosed CRAR weakness, RBI action-zone entry, and eventual default. The funding link is unobserved, not absent. No market-price link is established.

The product boundaries matter: Seiche covers **system dollar-funding capacity**; LiquiLens covers **institution and lender balance-sheet risk**; Undertow covers market liquidity and executable exit capacity. Undertow reports partial coverage across segments. Neither is evidence about Nedungadi’s historical route. See the [Seiche overview](https://api.seiche.info/api/overview) and [Undertow board](https://api.seiche.info/undertow/board.json).

The decisive limits are construction-PIT historical status, no real-money eligibility, no bitemporal input contract, proxy timing that can leave lead times optimistic, no authorised market-derived tier evidence, and unscoreable funding evidence for Nedungadi. Missing evidence is not calm. It is a boundary on what this replay can claim.

articles.headline: First Leasing replay: when a public balance-sheet radar cannot see through the record
articles.dek: First Leasing Company Of India’s fraud-masked default is not an early-warning success. It is a boundary case showing why a filing-period signal, a market-price signal and a model derivation must not be treated as the same evidence.
articles.body_markdown:
*Historical replay — not current news and not a forecast.* First Leasing Company Of India defaulted on 2013-12-02. The useful lesson is not that a public screen called the event. The supplied record does not establish that it did. Rather, it shows a harder limitation: an institution can be under severe economic pressure while its reported balance sheet fails to transmit that pressure to a threshold-based public-data system.

The distinction matters for the desk question: which balance sheet should feel stress first, and why? A filing-period signal describes what disclosed reports showed at an available reporting point. A market-price signal describes repricing in tradable instruments, when the market data are authorized for that use. A model derivation combines permitted inputs under a stated rule. None can be silently substituted for another; none proves the underlying economic condition by itself.

First Leasing is marked `fraud_masked` in this replay. Its case therefore tests the boundary of disclosed-data surveillance, rather than supplying evidence that an ordinary balance-sheet deterioration was identified in time.

## The record before the event

First Leasing Company Of India is classified as an NBFC, with default date 2013-12-02. Its PCA record contains no first action-zone date and no lead-month figure. Its funding record is scoreable, but contains no first signal and no lead-month figure. These are missing replay results, not affirmative findings that funding was calm, capital was adequate or the institution was safe.

The historical framework explicitly warns that institutions whose filings were later shown falsified can look compliant to a threshold engine; the forensic screen owns those cases. That warning is central here. The dossier does not provide underlying accounting particulars that would establish the route from misstatement to default. It does establish that the reported public record did not produce an earlier PCA action-zone entry or funding signal in this replay.

The India evidence is broader but tightly qualified. It covers 48 institutions across two decades, with a headline finding that 88.9% of non-fraud failures were flagged and median lead was 21.5 months. Yet its status is `PERIOD_END_PROXY_CONSTRUCTION_PIT`: it is not validated-backtest eligible, not real-money eligible and has no bitemporal input contract. Availability uses an explicit publication clock when present; otherwise it uses period end plus 60 days. The dossier says lead times are optimistic. These are diagnostic construction results, not tradable performance evidence. See the [Failure Radar board](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/board), [validation record](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/validation) and [First Leasing replay](https://liquilens.in/replay/first-leasing-company-of-india/).

## What the lenses saw

The PCA lens is a public-disclosure replay of the RBI’s PCA/SAF tripwires. Among 15 failed institutions, 5 entered an action zone first, with median lead of 41 months. That is evidence that disclosed supervisory-style thresholds can be informative in some cases. It is not evidence that they identified First Leasing: its supplied PCA fields show no action-zone date and no lead time.

The funding lens is narrower because it requires a disclosed liability series. Of 15 failed institutions, 10 had liability disclosures; the funding signal fired first for 4, with median lead of 38 months. First Leasing is marked scoreable, yet no first funding signal is recorded. That is a non-result in the replay, not a clean bill of health.

A filing-period signal must also be separated from a model derivation. The published rule can fuse disclosed levels, deterioration, a funding flag, a forensic indicator and an authoritative market drawdown into a presentation tier. PD levels are corpus-fitted and prior-corrected to a ~0.25%/yr population base rate using King-Zeng. That makes them model outputs, not direct observations. The conformal alarm is retained only as a diagnostic: its historical tier wiring is suspended and it has no score or tier authority pending prospective revalidation.

A market-price signal is different again. The dossier describes Merton PD as a market repricing signal, not a calibrated failure frequency. For the current market layer, data are fresh and clocked, but display, model-gate and tier use are not approved; admitted canonical records are 0/25. Market information therefore cannot authorize a current tier in this record.

## Why the warning mattered

A reported balance sheet is supposed to connect asset quality, loss absorption and creditor confidence. If losses, impairment or other relevant conditions are not truthfully represented, reported capital and risk measures can remain clear of a threshold. If disclosure does not reveal why liability providers should reassess the institution, a funding lens may not fire either.

That is an inference about the limits of observable inputs, not a reconstructed account of First Leasing’s finances. The dossier supports the narrower conclusion: in a fraud-masked case, apparent compliance in disclosed data may be an artefact of the record rather than evidence of resilience. A missed signal in an honest, timely disclosure regime could challenge the threshold. A missed signal where filings were later shown falsified can instead show that the measured balance sheet was not a reliable map of the institution.

The strongest counter-case can defeat any inflated version of this thesis. Perhaps the framework is simply too weak to identify stress reliably. First Leasing has no recorded PCA or funding lead. Historical availability is sometimes proxied using period end plus 60 days, and the dossier expressly calls the lead times optimistic.

The hazard evidence is also limited. The panel has 205 rows, 9 events and 27 institutions; 179 censored or unusable rows were excluded. Leave-one-institution-out AUC is 0.752, with an interval of 0.338 to 1.0. On the same held-out rows, the heuristic AUC is 0.799, above the hazard AUC. The temporal test has AUC of 0.645, below the 0.65 diagnostic gate, and cannot promote construction-PIT diagnostics.

That critique means this replay cannot demonstrate that the radar would have protected a creditor, investor or supervisor. Nor can a `fraud_masked` label solve forensic identification after the fact. The defensible claim is smaller: the system reports the absence and limits of disclosed signals rather than converting unavailable or compromised evidence into reassurance.

## What today's board shares

The board as of 2026-09-25 has 0 red institutions, 1 orange, 3 yellow and 15 green; 21 stale institutions are excluded. Utkarsh Small Finance Bank is orange, based on a 2025-03-31 filing as-of date aged 18 months, with score 74.9. Belstar Microfinance Limited is yellow as of 2026-03-31, aged 6 months, score 77.8. Nothing older than 24 months is presented as current, while institutions without vetted dossiers are absent by design. ## The next falsifiable test

The thesis weakens if a genuinely bitemporal, prospectively audited sample finds that disclosed PCA, funding and forensic signals do not identify pressure before adverse outcomes better than chance. It gains credibility only if prospective records preserve what was knowable when, retain missing and stale observations instead of filling them with calm, and separately test filing signals, market-price signals and model derivations. This is not investment advice and not a credit rating.

## Follow the pressure chain

The disciplined sequence is reported assets and capital; disclosed liability structure; supervisory-style thresholds; forensic indicators; then market and exit conditions where authority permits. A break should prompt investigation, not automatic certainty.

LiquiLens covers **institution and lender balance-sheet risk**. [Seiche](https://api.seiche.info/api/overview) covers **system dollar-funding capacity**. articles.headline: Altico’s historical warning was funding dependence, not a forecast of failure

## The record before the event

Altico was an NBFC, its funding lens was scoreable, and the dossier records no fraud-masking designation. Its first funding signal was a 23.7 index reading in the stable band at the 2017-03-31 period end. The accompanying flag was explicit: **“CP reliance 29% (rollover-freeze exposure)”**. Those dates have separate meanings. The reporting period describes when the underlying filing-period measure was recorded. The knowledge-time proxy estimates when the information could have become available under the replay’s construction rule. The default date is the recorded outcome. Conflating them would turn a historical reconstruction into a claim about contemporaneous knowledge or tradable timing that the dossier does not support.

The narrow finding is that the reconstructed public record contains an NNPA breach before the recorded event. The dossier records no first funding signal. Neither finding establishes causation, and the fraud-masked status means a ratio-based reconstruction cannot be treated as a complete account of the institution’s condition.

## The record before the event

The [Failure Radar board](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/board) identifies New India Co-operative Bank’s first action-zone signal in FY2021. The named breach is NNPA, with a stated lead of 44 months to the recorded event.

This is a filing-period signal. It means a disclosed measure crossed a PCA/SAF-style tripwire in the reconstructed record. It does not show when management understood the underlying condition, when a supervisor acted, when depositors altered behaviour, or when any market incorporated information. Nor does it establish that the NNPA breach caused the event.

The 2021-05-30 date requires particular care. The availability rule uses an explicit publication clock when one is present; otherwise it uses period end plus 60 days. For this case, the date is a knowledge-time proxy generated by that rule, not a verified case-specific publication timestamp. Treating 2021-03-31 as the moment an investor could have acted would overstate the evidence.

Fraud masking is not a footnote. The dossier states that institutions whose filings were later shown falsified can appear compliant to a threshold engine, while the forensic screen addresses that problem. A detected breach therefore does not prove that the engine observed the whole condition, or that the disclosed series captured the decisive source of stress. It is the earliest recorded action-zone breach in this replay.

## What the lenses saw

The PCA/SAF lens saw NNPA. The funding lens records no first signal. That is non-firing or unavailable evidence, not affirmative evidence that liabilities were stable. The funding lens only sees institutions that disclose a liability series; lack of a recorded funding signal cannot be converted into a finding of benign funding.

The historical summaries retain that eligibility distinction. Of 15 failed institutions, 5 first entered an action zone, with a median stated lead of 41 months. Of the same 15 failures, 10 had liability disclosures; 4 had a funding signal fire first, with a median stated lead of 38 months. These describe different eligible subsets. A market-price signal is not part of the case thesis. The current market layer is sourced from Yahoo Finance daily closes, auto-adjusted, but no market-price reading is presented for this institution. The warning mattered because it located visible, disclosed asset-quality pressure before the recorded event. Under the quadrant rule, any RBI action-zone breach can place an institution in red. That is an operational classification rule, not a declaration that failure was inevitable.

The narrow thesis is that IL&FS’s disclosed funding condition appeared before a formal PCA action-zone signal in this reconstruction. It is a filing-period signal: an indicator assigned to a reporting period and placed on an estimated information clock. It is not a market-price signal. Nor is it a model derivation proving that funding weakness caused the event. IL&FS was scoreable on the funding lens. Its first disclosed funding signal is attached to **2015-03-31**, has index **45.4**, sits in the watch band, and has no listed flags. The replay uses explicit publication time where available; otherwise it uses period end plus **60** days. Measured from that proxy to **2018-08-28**, the dossier reports **38** months. The PCA replay, by contrast, records no first action-zone entry. The defensible conclusion is limited: under the reconstruction’s rules, the funding lens registered before a PCA action-zone event. The construction has a material missing-data boundary. The funding lens only observes institutions disclosing a liability series. Institutions without that series are not silently treated as healthy. ## What the lenses saw

The funding lens supplied the positive historical observation: watch first. The PCA lens supplied a contrasting observation: no first action zone. These are separate filing-based lenses, and neither should be recast as a live market verdict.

A balance-sheet interpretation is possible but remains a model derivation. If liabilities must be renewed while assets are difficult to turn into cash or depend on continuing finance, worsening funding resilience can create pressure before a disclosed solvency or action-zone threshold is crossed. That is a plausible pressure-chain hypothesis, not a fact established for every link at IL&FS. The replay establishes signal ordering and an event date; it does not reconstruct causation.

A funding watch can matter as an investigation-order signal. It says an analyst should examine disclosed liability resilience rather than wait for a formal threshold to settle the question. The fraud-masked flag is central rather than incidental. Filings later shown to be falsified can appear compliant to a threshold engine. This distinction also prevents a category error. It is not a model derivation, because the proposed liability-to-stress chain is an interpretation rather than an observed causal result.

The strongest counter-case can defeat the thesis. Its temporal diagnostic AUC is **0.645**, below the **0.65** gate, which it fails. The leave-one-institution-out row AUC is **0.752**, with a confidence interval from **0.338** to **1.0**; the heuristic AUC is **0.799** on the same held-out rows. Those results are too uncertain, and too construction-dependent, to promote this replay into a forecast engine.

## What today's board shares

Today’s board is not an extension of IL&FS’s outcome. As of **2026-09-12**, it contains **0** red, **1** orange, **3** yellow and **15** green institutions. Utkarsh Small Finance Bank is orange, with filings as of **2025-03-31**, age **18** months and score **74.9**. Belstar Microfinance Limited is yellow, as of **2026-03-31**, age **6** months and score **77.8**. ESAF Small Finance Bank is yellow, as of **2025-09-30**, age **12** months and score **66.0**.

Its market layer is dated **2026-09-11** and retrieved on **2026-09-12**, but has no admission, publication or tier authority. Rights approval, display approval, model-gate approval and tier-use approval are absent; admitted canonical records are **0/25**. See the [board record](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/board) and [market evidence index](https://api.liquilens.in/api/evidence/markets).

The thesis fails if prospective, genuinely time-stamped disclosures show that funding watches do not precede independently observed stress, or if PCA and forensic indicators arrive earlier with stronger out-of-sample performance. It also fails operationally where liability data are unavailable, stale or contradicted by verified later information. No signal in those circumstances means no measured signal, not safety.

A proper test needs a bitemporal input contract, actual publication times, pre-specified thresholds and a prospective outcome window. It should report separately on institutions with and without liability disclosures, retain fraud-masking cases rather than converting them into clean negatives, and publish the unavailable population. Until then, IL&FS remains historically suggestive ordering, not a tradable forecast.

Use LiquiLens for **institution and lender balance-sheet risk**: disclosed funding conditions, deterioration, forensic boundaries and tiers. Use Seiche for **system dollar-funding capacity**. CRAR and NNPA point to a plausible balance-sheet pressure chain. A capital-adequacy breach indicates less buffer against risk-weighted exposures. Third, no scoreable funding sequence exists for Global Trust Bank. Without it, the proposed progression from impaired assets to capital compression to creditor or depositor sensitivity remains a plausible chain, not a demonstrated chain. The correct use is an alert for investigation. It is not evidence that every CRAR-and-NNPA breach ends in default, and it is not evidence that institutions without a funding flag are safe.

## What today's board shares

As of 2026-09-10, the board contains 0 red, 1 orange, 3 yellow and 15 green institutions, while 21 stale institutions are excluded. Utkarsh Small Finance Bank is orange, using a filing as of 2025-03-31 aged 18 months. Belstar Microfinance Limited is yellow, using 2026-03-31 aged 6 months. ESAF Small Finance Bank is yellow, using 2025-09-30 aged 12 months.

These are current screening observations, not analogies to Global Trust Bank and not claims of failure. The [market evidence index](https://api.liquilens.in/api/evidence/markets) does not authorise market-derived display or tier use for every expected canonical record. A fresh market pack is therefore not interchangeable with a permitted market-price signal.

LiquiLens covers **institution and lender balance-sheet risk**. Seiche covers **system dollar-funding capacity** through its [overview](https://api.seiche.info/api/overview). Undertow covers **market liquidity and executable exit capacity** through its [board](https://api.seiche.info/undertow/board.json). These research boundaries are complementary, not licences to fuse unauthorised inputs into a single institutional verdict.

## The next falsifiable test

The thesis weakens if authentic, time-stamped pre-event disclosures show that Global Trust Bank had not breached the relevant CRAR and NNPA action-zone conditions by the stated knowledge time, or show that the recorded breach derives solely from later reconstruction rather than then-available information.

It strengthens if independently time-stamped liability disclosures show subsequent funding pressure consistent with the proposed chain. Either test must preserve original publication timing and identify falsified filings. Otherwise, apparent lead time remains potentially optimistic.

## Follow the pressure chain

Start with impaired assets and reported loss recognition. Ask whether those pressures compress capital. Then ask whether a reduced buffer affects confidence and whether liability pressure is independently observable. Do not reverse the sequence merely because funding distress is easier to narrate after a failure.

For current work, require fresh vetted public dossiers, remove stale, future-dated and unclocked readings from signal or tier authority, and treat absent liability disclosure as unknown. **Institutions without vetted dossiers are absent by design: nothing here is scored from memory.**

## Sources, method, and limits

The principal records are the [Global Trust Bank replay](https://liquilens.in/replay/global-trust-bank/), [Failure Radar board](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/board), [historical validation](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/validation), [market evidence](https://api.liquilens.in/api/evidence/markets), and [LiquiLens research](https://liquilens.in/research/). The [US NDFI diagnostic](https://api.liquilens.in/api/us-radar/ndfi) is separate context, not evidence about this institution.

Historical evidence remains PERIOD_END_PROXY_CONSTRUCTION_PIT; it is not validated-backtest eligible or real-money eligible; lead times may be optimistic; and fraud masking can make reported compliance misleading. The conclusion is limited to the earliest disclosed warning represented in this dossier: capital and asset quality, not a proven funding sequence.

articles.headline: Altico’s replay: a stable funding band can still contain a refinancing warning
articles.dek: Altico’s disclosed commercial-paper reliance was a filing-period signal of rollover-freeze exposure well before default. It is a useful historical clue, but the construction-PIT record cannot establish a validated predictive advantage.
articles.body_markdown:
*This is a historical replay, not current news and not a forecast. It examines Altico before its default date of 2019-09-12. The relevant filing period ended 2017-03-31, with a knowledge-time proxy of 2017-05-30. Current board and market material discussed below is separately as of 2026-09-08.*

The question is not whether Altico’s funding flag predicted its default. The dossier cannot support that claim. It can support a narrower observation: Altico’s first funding signal identified commercial-paper reliance of 29% and explicitly described rollover-freeze exposure, even though the funding index sat in a stable band. That contrast makes Altico a useful replay of a balance-sheet question: which institution should be investigated first when reported broad measures look calm but liabilities require recurring refinancing?

This is a screen for inquiry, not a conclusion about creditworthiness. It is **not a credit rating**, not investment advice, and not a prediction of institutional failure.

## The record before the event

Altico defaulted on 2019-09-12. Its recorded first funding signal belongs to the period ending 2017-03-31, with 2017-05-30 used as the knowledge-time proxy. The recorded lead was 27 months. The funding index was 23.7, its band was stable, and the disclosed flag was CP reliance of 29% with rollover-freeze exposure.

Those items are different kinds of evidence. The period-end balance-sheet observation is a filing-period signal. The knowledge-time proxy is an attempted estimate of when that signal could have been available, not proof of an exact public-information clock. The stable band is an output of a funding index. The rollover flag is a component-level warning. None is a market-price signal, and none is a calibrated probability that Altico would fail.

The [Altico replay](https://liquilens.in/replay/altico/) and [Failure Radar board](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/board) preserve this distinction. A stable aggregate band did not erase the disclosed funding feature; it meant that the broad index did not register a more severe state. The replay therefore argues against reading a single band as a clean bill of health.

## What the lenses saw

Altico’s funding lens was scoreable and fired first, with the recorded 27-month lead. The historical funding summary covers 15 failed institutions. Liability disclosures were available for 10, the funding signal fired first for 4, and the median lead was 38 months. These are descriptive replay results, not a validated backtest or a real-money record.

A separate regulatory-action lens gives a different picture. In the public-disclosure replay of RBI PCA or SAF tripwires, 5 of 15 failed institutions entered an action zone first, with a median lead of 41 months. The India diagnostic describes 48 institutions across two decades and reports 88.9% of non-fraud failures flagged, with a median lead of 21.5 months. These figures do not show that a funding flag dominates a supervisory threshold. They show that different disclosed lenses may register at different points in a failure sequence.

The historical record is explicitly `PERIOD_END_PROXY_CONSTRUCTION_PIT`. It is not validated-backtest eligible, not real-money eligible, and lacks a bitemporal input contract. Where an explicit publication clock was unavailable, the availability basis was period end plus 60 days. The dossier says lead times are optimistic. A filing-period value may therefore have been treated as knowable earlier than a user could have verified it.

The [historical validation record](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/validation) adds a further restraint. Its temporal diagnostic AUC was 0.645, below the 0.65 gate, and did not pass. The held-out comparison also reported a heuristic AUC of 0.799 against hazard AUC of 0.752 on the same rows. The model derivation is consequently diagnostic only; it cannot promote the construction-PIT evidence into a settled forecasting claim.

## Why the warning mattered

The warning mattered as a question about liability structure, not as proof of causation. The dossier’s own wording identifies rollover-freeze exposure. Commercial paper is therefore the specific disclosed channel worth examining in this replay: refinancing dependence can be important even when a wider funding index remains stable.

That conclusion should be kept at the level the evidence permits. Altico’s flag did not establish that refinancing pressure caused the default. The dossier does not provide an event-by-event account of funding withdrawals, asset sales, liquidity use, hidden losses, or misconduct. It does show a disclosed feature, a later default date, and a recorded lead under a proxy availability convention.

The more defensible lesson is about aggregation. A composite can summarize multiple inputs while a discrete component identifies a vulnerability the composite does not elevate. The filing-period signal is therefore a reason to inspect refinancing sensitivity; it is not a market verdict and not a model-derived failure frequency.

## The strongest counter-case

The counter-case can defeat an overconfident thesis. Altico may be an anecdote selected after the event. Its funding band was stable. Among failed institutions with the stated historical coverage, only 4 funding signals fired first, and only 10 of 15 had usable liability disclosures. The lens is conditioned by disclosure availability. Institutions without a liability series are not demonstrated to be safe; they are simply not observable through that particular lens.

Timing may also flatter the result. The dossier warns that period-end-plus-60-day availability can make lead times optimistic. Its hazard panel excluded 179 censored or unusable rows, while the temporal diagnostic did not clear its stated gate. Filings later shown to be falsified can look compliant to a threshold engine; the dossier assigns that limitation to a forensic screen. Altico is not fraud-masked, but the broader masking risk remains.

A serious reader can therefore reject the proposition that CP reliance reliably identifies the next failure. The evidence supports only a conditional investigative rule: where the disclosure exists, a rollover flag may deserve attention alongside, rather than instead of, other lenses.

## What today's board shares

Today’s board is not evidence about Altico’s past and must not be fused with the replay. As of 2026-09-08, the board reports 0 red, 1 orange, 3 yellow, and 15 green institutions; 21 stale institutions are excluded. Utkarsh Small Finance Bank is orange, based on 2025-03-31 material aged 18 months, with a score of 74.9. Belstar Microfinance Limited is yellow from 2026-03-31, aged 6 months, with a score of 77.8. ESAF Small Finance Bank is yellow from 2025-09-30, aged 12 months, with a score of 66.0.

These are published screen tiers, not ratings or forecasts. The stated rule can use levels, deterioration, funding flags, forensic indicators and, only when authoritative, market drawdown inputs. The [market evidence endpoint](https://api.liquilens.in/api/evidence/markets) is fresh by its pack clock, but has no publication, admission, knowledge, or tier authority. Rights and display approval were not granted for every expected canonical record. Freshness is not authorization, and this market layer cannot validate or rank a current institution here.

## The next falsifiable test

The Altico inference should fail if prospectively collected disclosures of short-term rollover dependence do not identify earlier subsequent funding strain than comparable disclosed balance sheets. It should also fail if actual publication timestamps remove the apparent lead created under the period-end-plus-60-day proxy.

A credible test would fix the funding definition before outcomes, use vetted public dossiers, record actual availability, and preserve the rule before observing subsequent events. It would need to improve on the disclosed heuristic in a future temporal sample. Until then, the replay remains a historical mechanism test, not a deployable prediction engine.

## Follow the pressure chain

The pressure chain begins with the liability mix and its refinancing requirement. Altico’s disclosed CP-reliance flag places attention on that requirement, but does not establish its later path. LiquiLens covers **institution and lender balance-sheet risk**. [Seiche](https://api.seiche.info/api/overview) covers **system dollar-funding capacity**; its composite was 44.9, EROSION, with guarded confidence because modelled or slow-moving structure led current market-plumbing confirmation. [Undertow](https://api.seiche.info/undertow/board.json) covers **market liquidity and executable exit capacity** and reports several segments as PARTIAL.

These are separate layers. They are not confirmation that Altico’s historical mechanism is active now, and no layer substitutes for another.

## Sources, method, and limits

Key dossier-linked materials include the [Failure Radar board](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/board), [validation record](https://api.liquilens.in/api/failure-radar/validation), [market evidence](https://api.liquilens.in/api/evidence/markets), [Altico replay](https://liquilens.in/replay/altico/), and [LiquiLens research](https://liquilens.in/research/).

Nothing older than 24 months is presented as current on the board; failed institutions are presented through replay evidence instead. Institutions without vetted dossiers are absent by design and are not scored from memory. Stale, future-dated, or unclocked market readings may remain visible but have no signal or tier authority. Missing liability disclosure is not safety, missing system context is not calm, and a historical replay is not a forecast.
